'''Bradley Adam Thiessen''' is an American statistician and academic administrator. He served as the interim president of the [[New College of Florida]] from January 2023 to March 2023.

== Life ==
Thiessen earned a bachelor's degree in secondary mathematics education at the [[St. Ambrose University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Delaney |first=Meghin |date=August 1, 2016 |title=New College names new director of institutional performance assessment |work=Bradenton Herald |url=https://www.bradenton.com/news/local/education/article93123282.html |access-date=2023-02-15}}</ref> He earned a master's degree and Ph.D. in educational measurement and statistics from the [[University of Iowa]].<ref name=":0" /> His 2008 dissertation was titled, ''Relationship between test security policies and test score manipulations''.<ref name=":3">{{Cite thesis |last=Thiessen |first=Bradley Adam |title=Relationship between test security policies and test score manipulations |date=2008 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=[[University of Iowa]] |oclc=317117606}}</ref> Timothy Neri Ansley was his doctoral advisor.<ref name=":3" />

Thiessen worked at the St. Ambrose University for 14 years as the university assessment coordinator and a faculty member in the department of mathematics and statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 1, 2016 |title=New College Hires Director for Brand-New Position |url=https://www.sarasotamagazine.com/news-and-profiles/2016/08/new-college-hires-director-for-brand-new-position |access-date=2023-02-15 |website=Sarasota Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> He joined the [[New College of Florida]] in July 2016 as the president's chief of staff, and a professor of statistics.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Irwin |first=Bonnie D. |date=December 16, 2019 |title=Announcement: Bradley Thiessen named as Director of Institutional Research |url=https://hilo.hawaii.edu/blog/chancellor/2019/12/16/bradley-thiessen/ |access-date=2023-02-15 |website=UH Hilo Chancellor's Blog |language=en-US}}</ref> In August 2016, he became its first director of institutional performance assessment.<ref name=":0" /> On January 2, 2020, he became the director of institutional research at the [[University of Hawaiʻi at Hilo]].<ref name=":1" /> On January 31, 2023, Thiessen was appointed as the interim president of the [[New College of Florida]] by the board of trustees, succeeding [[Patricia Okker]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Atterbury |first=Andrew |date=January 31, 2023 |title=Conservative trustees oust president at Florida's New College amid leadership overhaul |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2023/01/31/florida-new-college-conservative-trustees-00080541 |access-date=2023-02-15 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref> He served until March 2023 when he was replaced by [[Richard Corcoran]].<ref name=":2" />

In July 2024, Thiessen joined Florida Polytechnic University as interim provost.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Office of the Provost and Executive Vice President |url=https://floridapoly.edu/provost/index.php |access-date=2025-05-10 |website=floridapoly.edu |language=en}}</ref> On May 8, 2025, he was named Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs at Florida Polytechnic University.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Janelle Irwin |date=2025-05-08 |title=Brad Thiessen officially named VP of Academic Affairs at Florida Poly |url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/737170-brad-thiessen-officially-named-vp-of-academic-affairs-at-florida-poly/ |access-date=2025-05-10 |website=Florida Politics - Campaigns & Elections. Lobbying & Government. |language=en-US}}</ref>
